_source_of_truth: marketing/campaigns/peshta/final_polat_peshta_reel.mp4 (1080x1920, 30/1 CFR, 1290 frames, 43.000s). Frames win over every document.
_character_policy: M1 = male lead, F1 = female lead, CORPS_A = black-clad wide-brim-hat ensemble in the red studio, CORPS_B = white-robed hooded ensemble in the desert. All original fictional figures. No real person or series is named anywhere in this file.

_macro_boundary_correction.finding: The documented 11-window frame table is WRONG by a cumulative +1 per window. Every macro cut was bisected to the frame and photographed on both sides.
_macro_boundary_correction.note: Both tables sum to 1290, so the error is invisible to a checksum. Drift is +1 at the first cut and +10 by the last. This file uses the MEASURED boundaries; sub-shot frames therefore sum to the measured macro spans, not the documented ones.

_transitions.note: Incoming shot grows from a seed rectangle at f98 to full frame at f119. Both clips must cover f99-f118 for the compositor.
Left half holds 10a while the right half carries 10b; completes at f1116. Both clips must cover f1110-f1115.

_nmax_analysis.rule: a sub-shot of F frames at 30fps needs ceil(F*0.8) frames at 24fps; it exceeds N_max when F*0.8 > N_max
_nmax_analysis.conclusion: Zero sub-shots exceed any candidate N_max, including the worst case of 61. The editorial cut list is the only thing that sets the generation count; N_max does not add a single split.
